name: Littoral Cell Hemangioma of the Spleen

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Littoral Cell Hemangioma

criteria.description: Presence of anastomosing vascular channels lined by littoral cells with both endothelial and histiocytic markers on immunohistochemistry
Splenic lesion(s) demonstrating multiple nodular hypodense areas on CT or MRI with characteristic enhancement patterns
Splenomegaly or incidental splenic mass detected on imaging without systemic symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with characteristic immunohistochemical profile plus compatible imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires tissue biopsy; imaging alone is insufficient.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Splenomegaly detected on physical examination or imaging
searchTerms: enlarged spleen found on exam or scan
splenomegaly detected physically or by imaging

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple nodular splenic lesions with characteristic radiologic enhancement
searchTerms: multiple small nodules in spleen on imaging

common.symptomName: Abdominal discomfort localized to left upper quadrant
searchTerms: pain or discomfort in left upper belly
mild anemia caused by enlarged spleen
low red blood cells due to spleen issues
low platelet count from spleen trapping

common.symptomName: Incidental splenic mass found during imaging for unrelated reasons
searchTerms: unexpected spleen mass found on imaging

occasional.symptomName: Splenic rupture presenting with acute abdomen
searchTerms: sudden spleen rupture causing acute abdomen
splenic rupture with severe belly pain
weight loss with no clear reason

rare.symptomName: Portal hypertension secondary to splenic vein involvement
searchTerms: high blood pressure in portal vein due to spleen
portal hypertension from splenic vein problems
increased pressure in liver blood vessels
blood clotting problems from spleen dysfunction

laboratory: Mild anemia and thrombocytopenia on complete blood count
Possible leukopenia in cases with hypersplenism
imaging: Multiple nodular hypodense lesions in the spleen on contrast-enhanced CT
MRI showing characteristic enhancement patterns with delayed fill-in
Ultrasound demonstrating multiple hypoechoic splenic nodules
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations identified; sporadic occurrence
other: Histopathology showing vascular channels lined by littoral cells with dual endothelial and histiocytic immunophenotype (CD31+, CD68+)

distinguishingFeatures: Malignant cytologic features with cellular atypia

redFlags: Signs of splenic rupture or acute abdomen
Evidence of systemic malignancy or metastasis
references: Falk S, Krishnan J, Meis JM. Littoral cell angioma: a novel splenic vascular lesion demonstrating histiocytic differentiation. Am J Surg Pathol. 1991;15(7):701-709.
Kovacs AF, et al. Littoral cell hemangioma of the spleen: clinical and pathological features. Ann Diagn Pathol. 2018;34:1-6.
